evidence.excerpt: The project develops algorithms and tools for automatically constructing finite automaton models of communication protocols from network traffic, without access to protocol specifications. The main research directions are: improving the scalability of state-merging inference to protocols with large alphabets; integrating fuzzing-based counterexample generation into the inference loop; and establishing theoretical sample complexity guarantees for the resulting hybrid active-passive framework. A secondary objective is producing a verified automaton-based anomaly detector applicable to industrial control system traffic. The project involves collaboration with the School of Electrical Engineering in Belgrade and the Faculty of Informatics at Masaryk University in Brno. The team consists of four researchers at the University of Novi Sad plus two external collaborators.
